title: Decoding an encoded symbol
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a type, let $N\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $E$ be an injection from optional $\Gamma$-symbols into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits. For every optional symbol $a$, decoding its code $E(a)$ returns $a$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is an injection from optional symbols to blocks
replaced:
Let $E$ be an injection of $\Gamma \cup \{\text{blank}\}$ into blocks of $N+1$ optional
bits, and let the decoder be the associated left inverse of $E$. Then for every
$a \in \Gamma \cup \{\text{blank}\}$, decoding the block $E(a)$ returns $a$.
